text: The jack your headphones plug into is older than radio. <#0.5#> It began on a telegraph desk in eighteen seventy-seven, as a spring-jack: a wedge pushed between two pins to break a line. <#0.5#> Telephone exchanges borrowed it. But the wedge had to go in a certain way, so inventors made a plain round plug. <#0.5#> By the century's end, operators plugged their head receivers into jacks. <#0.5#> Marconi's radio patent came in eighteen ninety-six, nearly twenty years later. <#0.9#> Then radio came back for it. In nineteen sixty-nine, a standard for radio receivers described the small sockets your wired earbuds still use. <#0.6#> Older than radio, then written into a radio standard. Which old part is hiding in your pocket? <#1.0#>
